name: Cohen Tal
current_role: President, Nasdaq Inc. (leads Market Platforms / Market Services & Financial Technology)
profile: Tal Cohen is a President of Nasdaq, overseeing its North American and European markets plus its marketplace technology, surveillance and regulatory-reporting businesses. A market-structure veteran, he ran Chi-X Global (2010-16) and held senior roles at Instinet before joining Nasdaq in 2016 to run North American equities.
interesting_fact: Before Nasdaq he was CEO of Chi-X Global Holdings (2010-2016), an operator of alternative trading venues that competed with incumbent exchanges, and earlier co-headed electronic trading for North America at Instinet.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as an auditor at Arthur Andersen, is a certified public accountant (SUNY Albany BA, NYU Stern MBA), and sat on the board of Canada's IIROC regulator (2009-16) and the Canadian Depository for Securities (2013-16).
notes: Name in source is inverted ('Cohen Tal'). Best route is Nasdaq Corporate Communications (press center lists media contacts / 'Get in Touch'). Speaks at Georgetown Psaros Center FMQ events.

name: T Wilson Eglin
current_role: Chairman, CEO & President, LXP Industrial Trust (taken private by Brookfield/CPP Investments on Nov 2, 2026; post-close role unclear)
profile: T. Wilson (Will) Eglin has led LXP Industrial Trust (formerly Lexington Realty) as CEO since 2003, after joining as COO in 1993, and transformed it into a pure-play Sunbelt/Midwest industrial REIT. In July 2026 he agreed a $5.2B all-cash sale to Brookfield and CPP Investments, which closed on Nov 2, 2026.
interesting_fact: He steered LXP's multi-year pivot from a diversified net-lease REIT to a pure-play industrial owner (~53M sq ft in 12 markets), which culminated in the $5.2B take-private by Brookfield and CPP Investments in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: At Nareit REITweek in June 2026 he said 'The greatest opportunity for us is development in our land bank'; he has been with the company since 1993 and a trustee since 1994.
notes: LXP is now private (acquired by Brookfield & CPP Investments, closed Nov 2, 2026); LXP assets now managed by BGRE (bgre.com). IR email may lapse post-deal; Brookfield comms contact listed in the deal release. Unclear whether Eglin remains post-close.

name: Aaron A. Robertson
current_role: Director, Commercial Bancgroup, Inc. (NASDAQ: CBK) and Commercial Bank, Harrogate, Tennessee
profile: Aaron A. Robertson is a director (since Jan 2023) and major shareholder of Commercial Bancgroup, the Harrogate, Tennessee bank holding company controlled by the Robertson family and founded by E. Oscar Robertson in 1976; the company IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2025. Outside the bank he runs a cattle/farming business, works with Harrogate Insurance Agency and is a partner in Harrogate Restaurant Group.
interesting_fact: Commercial Bank was founded in Harrogate, Tennessee in 1976 by the late E. Oscar Robertson and remained Robertson-family controlled until its 2025 Nasdaq IPO.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong Claiborne County, Tennessee resident, he studied Diesel Technology at Southeast Kentucky Community & Technical College and has been self-employed in farming and cattle since 2009.
notes: Low public profile; family bank insider rather than an operator/entrepreneur in the podcast's sectors. Only route found is company IR.

name: Daryl Kenningham
current_role: President & CEO, Group 1 Automotive (NYSE: GPI); director, Darden Restaurants
profile: Daryl Kenningham has been CEO of Group 1 Automotive, the Fortune 300 Houston-based auto retailer with dealerships in the US and UK, since January 2023, after joining in 2011 as a regional VP and running US operations from 2017. A 30+ year auto-industry veteran, he previously was COO of Ascent Automotive and held roles at Gulf States Toyota and Nissan.
interesting_fact: Named one of Houston Business Journal's Most Admired CEOs of 2024; he also sits on the boards of Darden Restaurants and the Greater Houston Partnership.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1988 at Nissan Motor Corporation in sales, marketing and vehicle-distribution roles in both the United States and Japan; he also serves on the Capital Committee of Houston charity Kids' Meals.
notes: Business Roundtable member (businessroundtable.org/members/daryl-kenningham). Best route is Group 1 IR / corporate communications.

name: Michael Cloonan
current_role: President & CEO and director, Sionna Therapeutics (NASDAQ: SION); director, bluebird bio
profile: Mike Cloonan has run Sionna Therapeutics, a Boston-area biotech developing NBD1-stabilizer medicines for cystic fibrosis, since 2021 and took it public on Nasdaq in 2025. Previously COO of Sage Therapeutics and a long-time Biogen commercial leader (SVP U.S. Commercial), he began as a Bain & Company healthcare consultant. In Sept 2026 Sionna said it will advance its SION-451 + SION-2222 combination into Phase 2a.
interesting_fact: Sionna's science targets NBD1, a domain of the CFTR protein long considered 'undruggable', aiming at higher efficacy than existing CF modulators; Cloonan has discussed this journey publicly ('Drugging the Undruggable').
deep_cut_fact: A College of the Holy Cross graduate with a UVA Darden MBA, he has said on a podcast that his background is business rather than science, which is why Sionna's scientific founders brought him in to run the company.
notes: Media contact Sarah Spencer, IR contact Juliet Labadorf per 2026 releases. Avoid referencing the Aug 2026 Phase 2a SION-719 miss; company has since pivoted to the SION-451 combination.

name: James J Lynch
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Patriot Financial Partners (bank-focused private equity, Radnor PA); Patriot funds are >10% owners of USCB Financial Holdings
profile: James J. Lynch is a veteran Pennsylvania banker who co-founded Patriot Financial Partners in 2007 with W. Kirk Wycoff and Ira Lubert to invest in community banks; he appears as a 10% owner of Miami-based USCB Financial Holdings through the Patriot funds. Earlier he was Vice Chairman of Sovereign Bancorp, CEO of Sovereign's Mid-Atlantic Division, and ran Fleet Bank (PA/South NJ), Summit Bank and Prime Bank.
interesting_fact: Before private equity he ran a string of regional banks: Chairman/CEO of Prime Bank and Summit Bank in Pennsylvania, President/CEO of Fleet Bank in PA and South Jersey (2001-02), then Vice Chairman of Sovereign Bancorp (2005-07).
deep_cut_fact: As Patriot's board representative he has sat on the boards of several portfolio banks, including Heritage Oaks Bancorp (California), Cape Bancorp and Palmetto Bancshares.
notes: Identity based on SEC filings (USCB 13D/Form 4 list him as Patriot GP). Patriot's own website could not be reached to confirm a published contact; aggregator profiles mention LaSalle University trustee (past chair) and Union League of Philadelphia board but not verified from a primary source. Low public profile.
